query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a machine-learned interatomic potential (e.g., a neural-network potential) trained on ab initio liquid snapshots will significantly expand the accessible phase-space overlap between reference and target calculations, thereby reducing the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch compared to standard EAM references in high-entropy alloys at and near their high melting temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: A multicomponent high-entropy alloy (up to five principal elements) in the solid and near-liquid states at temperatures approaching the melting range (approximately 1400–2000 K).
generation.intervention: Replace the EAM-based reference in TOR-TILD or similar free-energy methods with a machine-learned potential trained on ab initio data from liquid configurations of the same multicomponent alloy.
generation.conditions: This intervention is applied over the composition range typical of multi-principal-element alloys (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi or similar systems) and temperatures within ±200 K of the melting point, ensuring sufficient thermal sampling of liquid and near-liquid configurations.
generation.structural_mediator: The machine-learned reference potential more accurately captures highly variable coordination and bonding environments encountered in disordered, high-entropy liquid structures, bridging the gap between classical reference potential coverage and ab initio complexity.
generation.mechanism: By training on ab initio data specifically collected for liquid-like configurations, the new reference potential reduces the extrapolation required during free-energy integration, lowering the bias from missing configurations in EAM references. This improvement arises from increased transferability of structural descriptors and on-the-fly refinement during sampling.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable reduction (likely on the order of 25–40% or more, but exact magnitude remains uncertain) in the free-energy discrepancy between reference-based and fully ab initio calculations, demonstrated through better consistency of ensemble-averaged properties in the liquid phase.
generation.baseline: Existing TOR-TILD free-energy calculations using EAM references show larger systematic errors in predicting high-temperature or liquid-phase free energies for many-component alloys.
generation.boundary: The proposed machine-learning approach is expected to be effective for high-entropy alloys in their solid–liquid range. For temperatures or compositions far outside the training set (e.g., extremely off-stoichiometric or well below 1000 K), the method may lose accuracy.
generation.uncertainty: Exact gains depend on the fidelity of the training set covering key liquid microstates; poor sampling could undermine improvements. Residual errors might arise from force-field functional limitations or missing rare events in the training data.

falsification_experiment.design: Compute the free energy via both (1) the proposed machine-learned reference method and (2) direct ab initio integration for a target high-entropy alloy (e.g., CoCrFeMnNi) at and near the melting temperature. Vary the relative occupancy of principal elements to test the method’s robustness.
measurements: Compare free energies from both methods across a temperature window of ±200 K around the melting point.
Examine radial distribution functions, mean-squared displacement, and short-range order metrics to confirm overlap in the phase space sampled by each method.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the machine-learned approach fails to reduce the free-energy discrepancy relative to EAM-based references by a statistically significant amount under standard confidence intervals in more than 50% of tested compositional variations, the hypothesis is falsified.
